A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProDAG by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the renumbered theoretical results.

before.justification: v2 reports original runtime measurements, linear and nonlinear synthetic experiments in Figures 1–4, and Sachs flow-cytometry results in Table 1.

after.justification: v4 retains original synthetic and real-data results and adds BOSS comparisons and three robustness experiments in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The projection-based distributions, acyclicity solver, variational objective, and nonlinear neural-network extension are retained. Algorithm 2 elaborates the existing Duchi projection step, while Appendix D newly discloses thresholding; neither is identified as a revision to the implemented method.

E1.justification: v4 substantially broadens the synthetic test scenarios beyond Gaussian-noise Erdős–Rényi graphs. Appendix F adds denser graphs, Gumbel-noise data, and scale-free graphs. The original linear, nonlinear, and Sachs coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 replace PC with BOSS in the linear comparisons. DAGMA, DiBS, DiBS+, and BayesDAG remain. Comparator membership in the nonlinear experiment and Sachs Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces controlled 20-node evaluations that double the edge count from 40 to 80 or vary noise and graph generation. These extend the evaluation design while retaining the established sample-size sweep and metrics. Existing validation splits, network configurations, and particle counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix F and Figures 5–7 explicitly test sensitivity to graph density, noise distribution, and graph family. v2 contains no corresponding robustness suite, so v4 materially expands the evidence about dependence on simulation assumptions.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and standard errors over 10 independently generated datasets for the runtime and synthetic plots. The added figures follow the same practice; no increased repetition count, new seed policy, or statistical testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v4 replaces PC curves with BOSS results and adds four-metric comparisons for three robustness scenarios. For example, the new dense-graph experiment shows higher F1 for DAGMA than ProDAG at large sample sizes. Table 1 remains numerically identical, including ProDAG's 19.3 Brier score, 20.9 expected SHD, 0.33 F1, and 0.66 AUROC.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 becomes Theorem 3.1, and Propositions 1 and 2 become Propositions 6.1 and B.1. Their assumptions, statements, and proofs in Appendices A–C are substantively unchanged, as are the projection definitions, ELBO derivation, and cubic complexity bound.

C1.justification: Both versions claim direct distributions over sparse DAGs, scalable variational inference, support for linear and nonlinear SEMs, and competitive or superior inference. Abstract and conclusion edits preserve these contributions; the added experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 replaces the suggestion of approximately quadratic empirical scaling with practical runtime and applicability statements. Appendix D newly acknowledges residual cyclic edges and the need for thresholding. Appendix F interprets the added experiments as evidence of reliability across different simulation scenarios.

D1.justification: v4 adds projection pseudocode, discloses a 0.1 edge cutoff and n=100 for timing, supplies BOSS implementation information, and revises the reported CPU. It also replaces ProDAG's repository URL with '[redacted]' and removes baseline license labels. Algorithm 2 introduces a threshold formula inconsistent with the stated ℓ1 constraint; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

R1.justification: v4 adds Andrews et al. (2023) for BOSS and Toth et al. (2024) on structural marginalisation and autoregressive orders. BOSS is positioned as a discrete greedy-search comparator. The broader positioning against regularization and state-augmentation approaches remains.

P1.justification: v4 copyedits passages, changes terminology to 'projected distributions,' retitles subsections, divides the nonlinear discussion into Sections 6.2–6.4, adds Section 7.6 and Appendix F, and removes the checklist. The main section sequence and most explanatory content are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds three four-panel figures and an Algorithm 2 display, changes the document's typography and layout, moves Figure 1 into one column, and reformats Table 1. Linear comparison plots have revised legends and axis ranges, and the appendices are reflowed.

improvement.justification: The BOSS comparison, Appendix F robustness tests, and disclosure of numerical acyclicity limitations strengthen the paper. However, v4 removes the code pointer and introduces erroneous projection pseudocode: Algorithm 2's printed threshold maps two positive entries 3 and 2 with λ=2 to an output with ℓ1 norm 4. The PDFs do not establish whether this is only a documentation error. Stronger empirical support and less reliable implementation guidance coexist without a reliably assessable net quality improvement.
